meta.title: Bernardo Freguglia · Full-stack Engineer
meta.description: Full-stack developer with 4+ years of experience in React, Next.js, TypeScript, NestJS and applied AI (RAG, LLMs). B.Sc. in Computer Science from UFOP, Brazil.

hero.summary: I turn ideas into real products: multi-tenant platforms, rule-heavy scheduling, multi-property booking calendars and, lately, AI-powered systems. 4+ years in production, freshly graduated in Computer Science.

sheet.title: Who wields the keyboard
bio: I started in 2012 writing Minecraft plugins just to see what would happen. Since then, curiosity became a profession: a student-run consultancy, a scale-up, contract work and a startup, always on products used by real customers.

At Seazone I grew from intern to front-end developer on a vacation-rental management system with multiple user roles and complex permissions. Then, as a full-stack developer, I built the clinic scheduling engine at Anjos Guia and the front end of Centra's B2B platform.

I paused to finish my Computer Science degree at UFOP, where my thesis became an LLM-based recommendation framework with RAG. Now I'm back with the best of both worlds: product experience and a solid academic foundation.
traits: Clear communication with product, design and support
Management background (Marketing and HR at a junior enterprise)
Cares about polished interfaces and readable code
Fast learner: Vue, Bun, Elysia and AI in the last year
sheet.interests: Fan of the Diablo franchise (yes, you can tell), tabletop RPGs (Pathfinder 2e) and any game with a talent tree.

calendar.name: Grimoire of Stays
stats: Properties × dates grid with horizontal and vertical scrolling
+3 view modes: all, reservations or blocks
Sticky headers so you never lose your place
calendar.flavor: A thousand bookings, a single glance.
calendar.problem: The operations team needed to see occupancy for many properties at once, crossing dates, multi-channel reservations and blocks.
calendar.solution: I built the grid view: dates on top with horizontal scrolling, properties on the left with vertical scrolling, and filters to show only reservations or only blocks. Later I adapted the same foundation into the owner view.
calendar.learned: Rendering performance for large lists, scroll synchronization, and how a single screen can serve different user roles.

scheduler.name: Hourglass of the Oracle
stats: Matches professional, procedure, room and time
Only offers staff who can perform the procedure
scheduler.flavor: No slot is offered in vain.
scheduler.problem: Beauty clinics have limited rooms, staff with different skills and shifting hours. Manual scheduling caused conflicts.
scheduler.solution: I modeled scheduling as domain rules: for each procedure, find qualified professionals, intersect their shifts with clinic hours and drop slots with no free room. NestJS + PostgreSQL on the back end, Next.js on the front.
scheduler.learned: Domain modeling, testing rules against edge cases, and the value of keeping business rules apart from frameworks.

noshbyte.name: Tome of NoshByte
noshbyte.flavor: The oracle that knows what you want to eat.
noshbyte.problem: Generic food recommendations ignore restrictions, preferences and real reviews. Which LLM recommends best, and at what latency cost?
noshbyte.solution: I built a full-stack framework: ElysiaJS (Bun) back end with Drizzle and PostgreSQL, Clean Architecture and DDD; RAG with pgvector embeddings; Next.js front end with streaming chat. I evaluated 6 models with two LLM judges.
noshbyte.learned: End-to-end AI engineering: retrieval, prompting, LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, and quality/cost/latency trade-offs.

multistep.name: Scroll of Summoning
stats: Onboarding for hosts, agents and properties
multistep.flavor: Every field, a rune in its rightful place.
multistep.problem: Support staff registered hosts and properties through long, error-prone forms.
multistep.solution: I built create and edit forms, many of them multi-step, with per-step validation, clear messages and a review before submission.
multistep.learned: Form UX, schema validation, and how to cut rework for the support team.

seasonal.name: Masks of the Seasons
stats: Platform identity for Christmas, New Year and Easter
One switch applies to every clinic served
Campaigns go live without per-client rework
In the demo: the design-token approach
seasonal.flavor: One platform, many clinics, a new season.
seasonal.problem: Anjos Guia serves many clinics and salons from a single system. For every holiday, the business wanted the whole platform dressed for the season.
seasonal.solution: I adapted the system's visual identity for each seasonal campaign (Christmas, New Year, Easter), reflected across every clinic using the platform. The demo shows how clean this gets with design tokens.
seasonal.learned: Design tokens in practice, and how to reskin an entire product without touching every screen.

catalog.name: Merchant's Forge
catalog.flavor: From brick to counter in a few clicks.
catalog.problem: Centra wanted to digitize B2B construction-material sales with AI assistance and needed a reliable front end for retailers.
catalog.solution: I owned the front end: landing pages, the virtual catalog, product CRUD for the marketplace and the multi-tenant experience.
catalog.learned: Shipping fast without sacrificing quality at a startup, and keeping a lean design system with shadcn/ui.
